title: R' Pinchas Dedehuva
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Kohelet Rabbah 2:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Kohelet_Rabbah.2.2.4), Rabbi Pinchas Dedehuva says, “It is mixed—what joy does it produce?” Seder HaDorot holds that this is not the name of a city; rather, the reading should be “R' Pinchas said: This laughter is mixed.”[^1]

[Vayikra Rabbah 20:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Vayikra_Rabbah.20.3) similarly cites Rabbi Abba bar Kahana opening with “Of laughter I said, it is mad”: “If this laughter is mixed, what benefit does joy bring?” Hyman therefore calls the author of Sheva Chokhmot’s claim that it is the name of a city a mistake.[^2]

notes.text: The heading’s Dedehuva is retained as a name-form without deciding that it is a place. The checked TE text of Kohelet Rabbah has Rabbi Pinchas Didhuba with a similar saying, supporting its title at that quoted occurrence; it does not establish Hyman’s or Seder HaDorot’s proposed word division. סה״ד is the work Seder HaDorot. Its exact passage and the Sheva Chokhmot claim were not independently retrieved, so the proposed correction remains attributed to those writers. Their unverified occurrences keep R'.

The accepted text’s דחובא is read as native דחוכא, “laughter,” in the targeted notice on PDF pages 184–185 (printed 1017–1018). Native ב״כ and the matching full TE paragraph of Vayikra Rabbah support Abba bar Kahana in place of the accepted ב״ב. The English corrects those readings transparently without changing the accepted Hebrew. “Mixed” remains literal; the cited full story joins a wedding feast with a death, but that narrative has not been inserted into Hyman’s abbreviated quotation. The checked modern 20:3 is the matching passage, not proof of identical historical numbering.
